title: SMIC N+2 (7nm-class) process
summary: China's leading-edge logic process, achieved with older lithography and multi-patterning.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

SMIC's N+2 process produces 7nm-class logic using deep-ultraviolet immersion lithography with multiple patterning, the route behind Huawei's domestically made advanced chips. Without extreme-ultraviolet tools, each layer needs several exposures, which raises cost, lowers yield and limits volume. It is a strategic capability rather than a commercially competitive node.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Mass production
Estimated window 2023–2027
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

The gap to leading-edge foundries is now measured in cost and yield rather than in whether the node exists at all.

What Would Change The View

  • Yield improvement without EUV.
  • Capacity allocation between Huawei and other customers.
  • Tool and spare-parts access under controls.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
